videos.script:
Four of Vue's built-in components do things no template can do on its own. {{teleport}} Teleport draws part of a component somewhere else in the page, out of a box that would clip it.

{{dialog}} Then the dialog element, where the browser does the hard parts of a modal for you. The focus goes in, Escape closes it, and the focus comes back.

{{suspense}} Then Suspense, which waits for components whose setup awaits something, and shows a fallback meanwhile. You will also see the compiler keeping a component's place across an await, as lesson ten promised.

{{errors}} Then what happens when the waiting fails, and where to catch it.

{{transition}} Then Transition and TransitionGroup. Vue does not animate anything. It puts classes on and takes them off, and the stylesheet does the rest.

{{motion}} And last, the request some people make for less motion, honoured in one block of CSS. The planner's form moves into a dialog, and new sessions slide into place, unless you asked them not to.
